title: Man. Post. Cap. IV: PL — culpae vs poenae; satisfactoriae / castigationes
pass_a_gloss: PL. I distinguish evils. For some are of fault, others of penalty. Those God had forbidden by His law, He had not threatened: these He had threatened, but had not forbidden. But spiritual death or the privation of original righteousness is an evil of fault, not of penalty properly so called. The Major is therefore denied, if it is understood of evils of fault. Although not even when understood of evils of penalty is it universally true. For evils of penalty ought to be distinguished into those which are penalties, as they speak, satisfactory, and those which stand somehow as prison penalties and troubles, or as paternal chastisements. The law was threatening those former alone. But man incurs these latter through his sin, because on account of Christ's satisfaction space was given him for repenting, and he is treated by God as a boy-son is wont to be by a father.
pass_b_english: PL. I distinguish evils. Some are of fault, others of penalty. God had forbidden the former by His law; He had not threatened them. He had threatened the latter; He had not forbidden them. Spiritual death—or privation of original righteousness—is an evil of fault, not a penalty properly so called. So the major is denied if it means evils of fault. And even of penalty-evils it is not universally true. Penalty-evils must be split into those that are, as they say, satisfactory penalties, and those that stand somehow as prison pains and troubles, or as a father's chastisements. The law threatened only the former. Man falls into the latter by his sin because, for Christ's satisfaction, space was given him to repent, and God treats him as a father treats a boy.
source_text: PL. Distinguo mala. Alia enim sunt culpae, alia poenae. Illa Deus lege sua vetuerat, non comminatus fuerat: haec comminatus fuerat, non autem vetuerat. Est autem mors spiritualis seu privatio justitiae originalis malum culpae, non poenae proprie dictae. Negatur igitur Major, si de culpae malis intelligitur. Quanquam ne de malis quidem poenae intellecta universaliter vera est. Distingui enim debent mala poenae in ea quae sunt poenae, ut loquuntur, satisfactoriae, & ea quae se habent aliquomodo ut carceris poenae & molestiae, vel ut castigationes paternae. Illas solas lex comminabatur. Incurrit autem in has homo per peccatum suum, quia propter Christi satisfactionem datum est ei ad resipiscendum spatium, & tractatur a Deo, ut solet a patre filius puer.

choices.choice: Spiritual death = culpae not poenae; law threatens only satisfactory penalties
